title: Open Source AI: From Mess to Map

sections.heading: Everyday analogy - a community kitchen
sections.body:
Think of AI as a recipe. Closed AI is a secret restaurant dish. Open-source AI is a community kitchen where the recipe is shared.

Anyone can read it, taste-test it, and improve it. Open-source AI means the model code and weights are public to use and remix. A license is the permission slip that says how you can use it.

sections.heading: Why it exists
sections.body:
The field moves fast and feels messy. This guide exists to give clarity and cure FOMO.

It covers the full path:
- model evaluation means testing how good a model is before you trust it
- AI deployment means putting the model where people can actually use it

Open collaboration lets many people fix bugs and share improvements quickly.

sections.heading: What can go wrong
sections.body:
Sharing helps, but brings risks.

- a bad evaluation means you pick a model that looks good but fails in real life
- a bad deployment means it is slow, costly, or breaks with many users
- a confusing license means you think you can use it commercially when you cannot

Without checks, the mess gets worse, not better.

steps.narration: Start with a shared recipe: open model and its license tells you what is allowed.
Taste test it: evaluation checks if it actually works well.
Serve it: deployment puts it live for real users.
Community learns and writes a better recipe for next time.

quiz.q: What does 'open-source AI' mean in the kitchen analogy?
options: The recipe is secret and sold
The recipe is shared so anyone can read and improve it
Only one chef can taste it
You must pay to see the license
quiz.why: Open-source means code/weights are public with a license saying how to reuse.

quiz.q: What fails first if usage grows 100x after a weak deployment plan?
options: Deployment breaks: slow, costly, or crashes
quiz.why: Deployment covers serving at scale; without it, cost and speed fail first.

quiz.q: Why do we need model evaluation before deployment?
options: To test quality so we don't serve a bad model
To hide the model from the community
quiz.why: Evaluation tests how good a model is before trusting it live.
